params.body:
One button, two states, in the website widget that shows a dealer's stock on his own site.

Off it reads "Toon online voorraad". On it read **"Terug naar boven"**, which is a scroll instruction: it offers no way back to the dealer's own vehicles and does not look like the same button. Ilse reported it on 22 September 2026 as "de knop 'Toon online voorraad' is verdwenen", with Garage Heuten as the example. The button was there. Her dealer's settings were right too (`website_stocklist_integration` on, `default_all_vehicles` off), so the condition in R S2-5.4 was met; what she saw was the second state.

The French was wrong on top of that: "Retour à l'étage" is "back to the storey", a literal translation of the wrong meaning of "top".

## What changes

Both states now mirror each other, in the four languages the widget serves:

| | nl | fr | en | de |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| off | Toon online voorraad | Afficher le stock en ligne | Show online stock | Online-Bestand anzeigen |
| on | Verberg online voorraad | Masquer le stock en ligne | Hide online stock | Online-Bestand ausblenden |

## Why not "Toon enkel onze wagens"

That was the first version of this change and it was reverted before it landed. It describes the button perfectly, and that is the problem: **a visitor to a garage's website must not learn that the extra vehicles belong to other dealers.** "Toon online voorraad" has kept that quiet all along, and one possessive undoes it. So the labels speak about stock, never about whose stock it is.

That makes the wording here a requirement rather than a matter of taste, which is why `TheWidgetToggleSaysWhereItGoesTest` pins it: no ownership word in either state, in any of the four languages, and the second state is not a scroll instruction. Whoever rewrites this label later cannot quietly rewrite what the widget reveals about where the vehicles come from.

The translation key keeps its name, `show_only_own_vehicles`. A key lives in the code and not on the screen, and the gap between that name and the visible text is exactly how "Terug naar boven" survived unread for years.

## Also

R S2-5.4 now states both labels and the reason for them, and finding `de-knop-terug-naar-boven-zegt-niet-wat-ze-doet` records the report and the reverted first attempt.

Verified locally: `TheWidgetToggleSaysWhereItGoesTest` (4 tests, 106 assertions) and the rule-catalogue tests (`RulesIdentityTest`, `RulesCoverageTest`, `RulesDocsBuildTest`, `StylesheetSyntaxTest`, 12 tests) are green.
params.title: The widget toggle names its destination, never its owner
